reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism operates through a two-stage process: pre-training on synthetic datasets with known structure builds a generative model capable of producing symbolic expressions; inference-time refinement uses NGPQT to optimize the decoder weights based on observed data, effectively narrowing down the posterior distribution toward the most likely true equation. This dual approach allows for both broad structural learning and precise local adaptation. The use of NMSE as a differentiable loss function bridges the gap between continuous optimization and discrete symbolic generation, while policy gradients handle the non-differentiable token-to-equation conversion. The system assumes that the pre-training phase adequately covers the space of possible equations relevant to the domain, and that sufficient samples (10·d) allow accurate identification of d-variable functions. Failure modes include overfitting due to insufficient diversity in pre-training, poor convergence in NGPQT, or inability to generalize beyond the trained variable dimensions.
